technologies.name: HyDiffuse (rHuPH20-based SC delivery platform)
technologies.stage_raw: Preclinical / Platform (composition patents registered for 11 antibody drugs; lead standalone enzyme product HYDIZYME in BLA review at MFDS)
technologies.concentration_text: Not disclosed numerically as mg/mL; nonclinical PK data show HyDiffuse co-formulation increases Cmax by ~113-170% and AUC by ~117-162% vs. the antibody alone, across the 11 antibodies studied
technologies.mechanism: Proprietary recombinant human hyaluronidase (rHuPH20)-based platform, positioned as an independently developed competitor to Halozyme's ENHANZE, Alteogen's ALT-B4/Hybrozyme, and Samsung Bioepis' PH20-based technology. Temporarily degrades subcutaneous hyaluronic acid to enable diffusion/absorption of a co-administered antibody, permitting IV-to-SC conversion. Domestic (Korea) and international (PCT) composition patents now registered covering SC co-formulations with 11 named antibodies: pembrolizumab, bevacizumab, obinutuzumab, ramucirumab, donanemab, isatuximab, durvalumab, dostarlimab, cetuximab, risankizumab, and dupilumab -- the dupilumab entry directly overlaps this tracker's Dupixent benchmark. Separately, Huons Lab's standalone rHuPH20 enzyme product HYDIZYME is in BLA review at Korea's MFDS.

technologies.name: LEQEMBI IQLIK (lecanemab-irmb SC autoinjector formulation)
technologies.stage_raw: Approved / Commercially available (SC maintenance dose approved Aug 2025; SC initiation dose approved 2026-07-13; initiation-dose autoinjector commercially launched in the US 2026-08-24)
technologies.concentration_text: SC formulation 200 mg/mL (vs. 100 mg/mL for the IV formulation); 500 mg initiation dose given as two 250 mg/1.25 mL injections, each delivered in ~15 seconds; 360 mg/1.8 mL autoinjector used for maintenance dosing
technologies.mechanism: High-concentration (200 mg/mL) aqueous liquid formulation of lecanemab-irmb (anti-amyloid-beta protofibril monoclonal antibody) -- roughly double the concentration of the approved IV formulation (100 mg/mL) -- delivered via a single-dose prefilled autoinjector in approximately 15 seconds per injection. No hyaluronidase or particle/suspension technology involved: a straightforward high-concentration liquid reformulation paired with a fast, fixed-needle autoinjector device, enabling at-home SC initiation and maintenance dosing as an alternative to IV infusion. Included as an external cross-indication benchmark (Alzheimer's disease, not oncology/immunology) for a commercially-validated high-concentration mAb SC delivery technology.

deals.summary: Eisai and Biogen announced that LEQEMBI IQLIK (lecanemab-irmb) autoinjector is now commercially available in the U.S. for SC initiation therapy in early Alzheimer's disease: 500 mg given once weekly as two consecutive 250 mg/1.25 mL injections, each delivered in approximately 15 seconds. This follows FDA approval of the initiation-dose sBLA on 2026-07-13 (out-of-window for this run; context only) and is separate from the SC maintenance-dose formulation (360 mg/1.8 mL) approved in August 2025. SC formulation is 200 mg/mL vs. 100 mg/mL for the IV formulation. Patients may switch between IV and SC administration at any point in the treatment course. NEW ENTITY - first log of Eisai/Biogen lecanemab in this tracker; included as an external cross-indication (Alzheimer's, not oncology/immunology) benchmark for commercially-validated high-concentration mAb SC autoinjector delivery.

technologies.name: Subcutaneous High-Concentration Co-formulation Platform
technologies.company: Alphamab Oncology (Jiangsu/Suzhou Alphamab Biopharmaceuticals; 康宁杰瑞制药)
technologies.stage_raw: Commercial (lead product Envafolimab/KN035 approved 2021); platform extension JSKN033 in Phase III (CDE-approved Aug 2026)
technologies.concentration_text: Not disclosed numerically; described qualitatively as enabling 'high concentration' co-formulation, administered 'in tens of seconds', independent of hyaluronidase
technologies.mechanism: Proprietary high-concentration SC co-formulation platform enabling subcutaneous injection of large-molecule biologics (mAbs, bispecific ADCs) without a co-formulated hyaluronidase enzyme. Lead validation: Envafolimab (KN035), described by the company as the world's first SC-injected PD-L1 inhibitor, approved 2021. Platform extended to JSKN033 (HER2 bispecific ADC JSKN003 [DAR4, site-specific glycan conjugation of a topoisomerase I inhibitor] co-formulated with envafolimab PD-L1), now CDE-approved for Phase III (JSKN033-301) in recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer (announced 2026-08-03). Also underlies JSKN016 (TROP2/HER3 bispecific ADC), which has an ongoing SC-formulation Phase Ib (China) / Phase I (Australia) program, licensed globally (ex-Greater China) to Pathos AI in a deal announced 2026-08-03/04.

deals.summary: China's Center for Drug Evaluation (CDE) approved initiation of a Phase III study (JSKN033-301) for JSKN033, described by Alphamab Oncology as a first-in-class high-concentration SC co-formulation of a HER2 bispecific ADC (JSKN003; DAR4; site-specific glycan conjugation of a topoisomerase I inhibitor) with envafolimab (PD-L1 inhibitor). Trial: open-label, randomized, controlled, multicenter study of JSKN033 monotherapy vs. physician's-choice chemotherapy in recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer after platinum-based chemo/immunotherapy, irrespective of HER2 expression status. Company states the co-formulation is administered 'in tens of seconds' and is independent of hyaluronidase. No numeric concentration (mg/mL) disclosed in available coverage.
deals.molecule: JSKN033 (JSKN003 HER2 bispecific ADC + Envafolimab/KN035 PD-L1 inhibitor)

deals.summary: Pathos AI licensed JSKN016 (a first-in-class TROP2/HER3 bispecific ADC) from Alphamab Oncology, gaining exclusive development/commercialization rights outside Greater China (Alphamab retains Chinese-territory rights). Terms: $125M non-refundable upfront + up to $2,093M in development/commercialization milestones + tiered royalties (high-single to low-double-digit % of net sales). Both IV and SC formulations of JSKN016 are covered; an SC formulation of JSKN016 is already in Phase Ib (China) and Phase I (Australia) trials. CAVEAT (per soul-file 'never guess' rule): the primary source does not explicitly confirm whether Alphamab's proprietary SC high-concentration platform IP itself transfers under this deal, or only rights to the JSKN016 molecule/its existing SC-formulated clinical material -- logged with this ambiguity flagged rather than assumed.

technologies.name: Samsung Bioepis proprietary PH20-based SC conversion technology
technologies.concentration_text: Not disclosed numerically; enables IV-to-SC conversion of high-dose antibody drugs (previously only low-dose SC conversions achieved via concentration adjustment alone)
technologies.mechanism: CORRECTED 2026-07-28: WIPO/KIPO's International Search Report (ISR) and Written Opinion of the International Searching Authority (ISA) gave both underlying patents (WO2026/142299, WO2026/142300) a preliminary negative opinion on novelty and inventive step, citing prior Huons Lab, Alteogen, and Halozyme prior art plus a 2012 US patent as anticipating/rendering obvious the claims. Samsung Bioepis and industry sources characterize both as hyaluronidase manufacturing/purification (CMC) patents, not composition-of-matter or SC-platform patents; company states no separate platform-commercialization plan exists and no target product is finalized. Preliminary opinion only - national-phase claim amendments remain possible. See Deals_News_Feed row samsungbioepis_isr-novelty-rejection_2026-07-14 for detail. ORIGINAL SUMMARY RETAINED: Proprietary in-house recombinant human hyaluronidase (PH20-based), independently developed (own hyaluronidase, cultivation, and purification processes) and distinct from Halozyme's rHuPH20 (ENHANZE) and Alteogen's ALT-B4 (Hybrozyme). Temporarily breaks down the physical barrier of subcutaneous tissue to enable SC conversion of high-dose antibody drugs. Samsung Bioepis' prior SC conversions (Benepali SC/Enbrel biosimilar, Imraldi SC/Humira biosimilar) were low-dose and needed only concentration adjustment; this hyaluronidase-based technology targets high-dose blockbusters. Being positioned for the company's Keytruda (pembrolizimab) biosimilar and Enhertu (trastuzumab deruxtecan ADC) biosimilar programs. Two WIPO patent publications (WO2026/142299, WO2026/142300) covering hyaluronidase purification surfaced 2026-07-14, firming up the primary IP basis for this technology (see Deals_News_Feed).

deals.summary: Trade press reports both Samsung Bioepis and Celltrion are pursuing SC-converted biosimilars of Keytruda (pembrolizimab), targeting an estimated $12.7B Keytruda SC market opportunity as the reference product's patent protections face expiry; Celltrion is pursuing this via its own in-house proprietary hyaluronidase SC platform (the same underlying technology used for Herzuma SC/CT-P6 SC, tracked separately under Technology ID celltrion_herzuma_sc).

FLAGGED 2026-07-28 (out-of-window source used per Gate D correction exception; original reporting dated 2026-07-14, surfaced during this run's search, not previously logged): Per Pharm Edaily exclusive reporting citing the WIPO PCT international publication plus the Korean IPO's International Search Report (ISR) and Written Opinion of the International Searching Authority (ISA), the two Samsung Bioepis hyaluronidase-purification patents already tracked here (WO2026/142299, WO2026/142300; both filed 2025-12-23, internationally published 2026-07-02) received a preliminary negative opinion on novelty and inventive step. WO2026/142299 (removal of truncated hyaluronidase): claims 1-53, 56, 58-67 found to lack inventive step, with the ISA citing a prior Huons Lab patent as anticipating the core claims, and finding the multimodal-chromatography claims (5-7) obvious in view of Huons Lab + Alteogen prior art. WO2026/142300 (caprylic acid + depth filtration impurity removal): claims 1-51 found to lack inventive step, citing a 2012 US prior patent for the caprylic-acid/depth-filtration combination and Halozyme prior art for its hyaluronidase application; a composition-of-matter claim (hyaluronidase with HCP <100ppm) was found not novel either, since the ISA found the resulting substance indistinguishable from known hyaluronidase regardless of manufacturing process. Samsung Bioepis and industry sources characterize both patents as hyaluronidase manufacturing/purification (CMC) patents, not composition-of-matter or platform patents; Samsung Bioepis states it has no separate SC-platform commercialization plan and has not finalized a target product. This is a preliminary ISR/ISA opinion only, not a final rejection - claims can still be amended in national-phase prosecution. Directly qualifies the competitive-threat framing of the already-tracked WIPO-disclosure row (samsungbioepis_ph20_disclosure_2026-07-13) and market-analysis row (samsungbioepis_celltrion_keytruda-market_2026-07-14): the underlying IP, as currently claimed, appears weaker than the market reaction (Alteogen shares fell 2026-07-13/14) implied.

CORRECTED 2026-07-15: firmed up with primary-source detail. WIPO published two international patent applications from Samsung Bioepis in early July 2026 covering hyaluronidase purification/manufacturing: WO2026/142299 (method for removing cleaved/truncated hyaluronidase) and WO2026/142300 (method for removing impurities via caprylic acid treatment and depth filtration). No specific target product named. Following public reporting of this on 2026-07-14, Alteogen issued a same-day rebuttal statement asserting its ALT-B4 is a materially different substance from any PH20-based enzyme and that products combining pembrolizimab with ALT-B4 (Keytruda Qlex) are protected until 2043, arguing biosimilar competitors could not lawfully substitute a different hyaluronidase. Alteogen shares fell intraday on 2026-07-13/14 on the news. Samsung Bioepis stated it has not finalized which product(s) the purification IP will be applied to and is not pursuing an external platform-licensing business.

technologies.name: Hypercon (ex-Elektrofi)
technologies.concentration_text: Up to 500 mg/mL
technologies.mechanism: Water is extracted from antibody-solution droplets, precipitating the protein into smooth, dense microparticles which are then suspended in a non-aqueous carrier. Removing water from the particle core, rather than diluting the protein in more liquid, is what allows concentration well beyond what a liquid formulation can hold. Demonstrated injectable in ~20 seconds at <20 N glide force through standard SC needles.

technologies.name: IVL-BioFluidic (microfluidic/microsphere-based SC platform)
technologies.concentration_text: 750 mg/mL demonstrated, injected in 1-2 minutes
technologies.mechanism: Microfluidics-derived microsphere/microparticle drug delivery platform that enables ultra-high-concentration SC dosing without a co-formulated hyaluronidase enzyme. Targeted at monoclonal antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), and bispecific/fusion proteins.

deals.summary: First public disclosure of IVL-BioFluidic platform at BIO USA 2026; company reports 750 mg/mL achievable in a 1-2 minute injection without hyaluronidase.

Inventage Lab raised KRW 98.5 billion (~$69M), exceeding its KRW 80B target by 23%, with strong re-participation from existing mezzanine/pre-IPO investors. CEO Kim Ju-hee stated funds will accelerate advancement of the company's DDS platforms (including IVL-BioFluidic) and build out GMP production infrastructure.

technologies.name: Tiantan Weian (20% subcutaneous immunoglobulin - SCIG)
technologies.company: Chengdu Rongsheng Pharmaceutical (China National Pharmaceutical Group / Sinopharm)
technologies.concentration_text: 20% concentration (200 mg/mL) - China's first approved product in this category
technologies.mechanism: Plasma-derived polyclonal immunoglobulin (not a monoclonal antibody) formulated at 20% concentration for home-based SC administration. Included for competitive/market context only - adjacent product category, not mAb drug substance.

deals.summary: China's first 20% subcutaneous immunoglobulin (SCIG) product approved by NMPA.

technologies.name: SnapShot (glassy surfactant / MoNi)
technologies.company: Surf Bio (acquired by Halozyme Therapeutics, Dec 2025)
technologies.stage_raw: Preclinical / Platform (feasibility demonstrated; Halozyme integration ongoing)
technologies.concentration_text: 600+ mg/mL - doses over 1,000 mg in a single standard autoinjector shot (Surf Bio's own claim). CONFLICTING: Halozyme's official post-acquisition statement (Jan 2026) and the independent peer-reviewed Sci. Transl. Med. data both cite up to/surpassing 500 mg/mL instead.
technologies.needle_size: Standard 27-gauge (per Stanford STM study); compatible with commercial autoinjectors
technologies.mechanism: Commercial surfactants (e.g. Tween) depress the glass-transition temperature of spray-dried protein microparticles, leaving soft, tacky surfaces that stick together and clog injection. Surf Bio's MoNi surfactant enriches at the particle surface during drying and keeps it glassy above room temperature, yielding free-flowing, injectable ultra-high-concentration suspensions. Same underlying science published by the Stanford Appel lab (bioRxiv 2024, peer-reviewed in Science Translational Medicine, Aug 2025) - SnapShot is that platform's commercial form.

deals.summary: Acquired by Halozyme, up to ~$400M ($300M upfront + up to $100M milestones). Halozyme's own official post-acquisition statement (Jan 28 2026, via pharmaphorum) describes the platform as enabling concentrations 'up to 500 mg/mL' - lower than Surf Bio's own pre-acquisition marketing claim of 600+ mg/mL.

Peer-reviewed Stanford-led study in Science Translational Medicine demonstrating spray-dried microparticle mAb suspensions surpassing 500 mg/mL, deliverable through a standard 27-gauge needle at clinically relevant force. This independent peer-reviewed figure (500+) is notably lower than Surf Bio's own marketing claim of 600+ mg/mL, and matches Halozyme's official post-acquisition statement.
deals.source_name: PR Newswire (Surf Bio) / Science Translational Medicine

technologies.name: Nanoforming (biologics nanoparticle platform)
technologies.stage_raw: Preclinical / Platform (first commercial exclusivity agreement signed)
technologies.concentration_text: Suspensions >500 mg/mL reported; enables IV-to-SC switch at >400 mg/mL; particle sizes down to 50 nm
technologies.mechanism: Controlled nanoparticle/microparticle formation ('nanoforming') of biologics (mAbs, peptides, other large molecules) into highly stable particles with tunable size, enabling ultra-high-concentration suspensions for SC or inhaled delivery.

deals.summary: CORRECTED 2026-07-15: exact date now confirmed as May 12, 2026, per Nanoform's own inside-information press release (previously flagged as year unconfirmed). First-ever exclusivity agreement for Nanoform's biologics nanoparticle technology, covering one clinically/commercially validated target receptor. $1M non-refundable fee for 1-year exclusivity, extendable one additional year.

technologies.name: Crystalomics
technologies.company: Althea Technologies (now part of Ajinomoto Bio-Pharma Services)
technologies.concentration_text: 250 mg/mL demonstrated with crystallized infliximab (vs. 10 mg/mL IV solution), ~96% volume reduction. Related crystalline-antibody-in-hydrogel variants report up to 315 mg/mL, 89-97% encapsulation efficiency.
technologies.mechanism: Crystallizes monoclonal antibodies (demonstrated on infliximab/Remicade) into stable crystalline suspensions; some formulation variants combine crystalline-protein stability with soft hydrogel particle encapsulation. Legacy platform - no recent (2025-2026) deal activity found.

deals.partner: N/A (platform technology paper, not a deal)
deals.summary: Technical whitepaper describing the Crystalomics platform, demonstrating 250 mg/mL crystalline infliximab (~96% volume reduction vs. 10 mg/mL IV). No recent (2025-2026) deal activity found tied to this platform.

technologies.name: Solvent-Dehydration Hydrogel Microparticles
technologies.company: Academic (MIT - Doyle Lab, Dept. of Chemical Engineering; not a commercial platform)
technologies.concentration_text: 360 mg/mL antibody-laden hydrogel microparticle suspension achieved via continuous solvent-based dehydration
technologies.mechanism: Continuous microfluidic synthesis of hydrogel microparticles where antibody precipitation occurs simultaneously with solvent-driven dehydration, encapsulating antibody at high concentration for SC suspension delivery. Distinct academic approach (MIT, published Nov 2025) from commercial platforms like Hypercon or Microglassification, though mechanistically related.

deals.summary: Peer-reviewed paper (Zheng, Attia, Teng, Doyle - MIT) in Advanced Materials demonstrating 360 mg/mL antibody-laden hydrogel microparticles via continuous solvent-based dehydration.

technologies.name: Sarclisa Escena (SC isatuximab, on-body injector)
technologies.concentration_text: Not disclosed; delivered via on-body injector rather than a concentration-enabling formulation technology
technologies.mechanism: FDA-approved subcutaneous reformulation of isatuximab (previously IV-only), administered manually or via an on-body injector across all approved IV indications in multiple myeloma. First anticancer agent approved via on-body injector; no hyaluronidase, particle, or crystalline technology disclosed - device-enabled rather than formulation-enabled.

deals.summary: FDA approved isatuximab-irfc (Sarclisa Escena) for subcutaneous injection, extending to all currently approved IV isatuximab indications in multiple myeloma. Administered manually or via an on-body injector. First anticancer agent approved via on-body injector.

recent_activity.summary: Huons Lab registered domestic (Korea) and international (PCT) composition patents covering SC formulations of 11 antibody drugs (pembrolizumab, bevacizumab, obinutuzumab, ramucirumab, donanemab, isatuximab, durvalumab, dostarlimab, cetuximab, risankizumab, dupilumab) co-formulated with its proprietary HyDiffuse rHuPH20 platform. recent_activity.summary: Eisai and Biogen announced that LEQEMBI IQLIK (lecanemab-irmb) autoinjector is now commercially available in the U.S. for SC initiation therapy in early Alzheimer's disease: 500 mg given once weekly as two consecutive 250 mg/1.25 mL injections, each delivered in approximately 15 seconds. This follows FDA approval of the initiation-dose sBLA on 2026-07-13 (out-of-window for this run; context only) and is separate from the SC maintenance-dose formulation (360 mg/1.8 mL) approved in August 2025. SC formulation is 200 mg/mL vs. 100 mg/mL for the IV formulation. Patients may switch between IV and SC administration at any point in the treatment course. NEW ENTITY - first log of Eisai/Biogen lecanemab in this tracker; included as an external cross-indication (Alzheimer's, not oncology/immunology) benchmark for commercially-validated high-concentration mAb SC autoinjector delivery.

recent_activity.summary: China's Center for Drug Evaluation (CDE) approved initiation of a Phase III study (JSKN033-301) for JSKN033, described by Alphamab Oncology as a first-in-class high-concentration SC co-formulation of a HER2 bispecific ADC (JSKN003; DAR4; site-specific glycan conjugation of a topoisomerase I inhibitor) with envafolimab (PD-L1 inhibitor). Trial: open-label, randomized, controlled, multicenter study of JSKN033 monotherapy vs. physician's-choice chemotherapy in recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer after platinum-based chemo/immunotherapy, irrespective of HER2 expression status. Company states the co-formulation is administered 'in tens of seconds' and is independent of hyaluronidase. No numeric concentration (mg/mL) disclosed in available coverage.

Terms: $125M non-refundable upfront + up to $2,093M in development/commercialization milestones + tiered royalties (high-single to low-double-digit % of net sales). Both IV and SC formulations of JSKN016 are covered; an SC formulation of JSKN016 is already in Phase Ib (China) and Phase I (Australia) trials. G2G Bio and Celltrion signed an MOU including a Material Transfer Agreement (MTA) for 'ultra-high-concentration antibody SC formulation platform technology cooperation.' Under the MTA, Celltrion will transfer antibody substance(s) to G2G Bio so the companies can evaluate applicability to G2G Bio's high-concentration microparticle platform 'InnoBioLAMP' (an extension of G2G Bio's existing InnoLAMP long-acting microsphere DDS technology into biologics/antibodies), with a view to joint R&D and potential commercialization if feasibility is confirmed. This is G2G Bio's first public disclosure of InnoBioLAMP and marks its formal entry into antibody biologics. Specific target molecule(s), research schedule, and cost-sharing terms not disclosed; actual SC-formulation conversion feasibility still to be confirmed via non-clinical/clinical testing per company statement.

recent_activity.summary: FLAGGED 2026-07-28 (out-of-window source used per Gate D correction exception; original reporting dated 2026-07-14, surfaced during this run's search, not previously logged): Per Pharm Edaily exclusive reporting citing the WIPO PCT international publication plus the Korean IPO's International Search Report (ISR) and Written Opinion of the International Searching Authority (ISA), the two Samsung Bioepis hyaluronidase-purification patents already tracked here (WO2026/142299, WO2026/142300; both filed 2025-12-23, internationally published 2026-07-02) received a preliminary negative opinion on novelty and inventive step. WO2026/142299 (removal of truncated hyaluronidase): claims 1-53, 56, 58-67 found to lack inventive step, with the ISA citing a prior Huons Lab patent as anticipating the core claims, and finding the multimodal-chromatography claims (5-7) obvious in view of Huons Lab + Alteogen prior art. WO2026/142300 (caprylic acid + depth filtration impurity removal): claims 1-51 found to lack inventive step, citing a 2012 US prior patent for the caprylic-acid/depth-filtration combination and Halozyme prior art for its hyaluronidase application; a composition-of-matter claim (hyaluronidase with HCP <100ppm) was found not novel either, since the ISA found the resulting substance indistinguishable from known hyaluronidase regardless of manufacturing process. Samsung Bioepis and industry sources characterize both patents as hyaluronidase manufacturing/purification (CMC) patents, not composition-of-matter or platform patents; Samsung Bioepis states it has no separate SC-platform commercialization plan and has not finalized a target product. This is a preliminary ISR/ISA opinion only, not a final rejection - claims can still be amended in national-phase prosecution. Directly qualifies the competitive-threat framing of the already-tracked WIPO-disclosure row (samsungbioepis_ph20_disclosure_2026-07-13) and market-analysis row (samsungbioepis_celltrion_keytruda-market_2026-07-14): the underlying IP, as currently claimed, appears weaker than the market reaction (Alteogen shares fell 2026-07-13/14) implied.

recent_activity.summary: CORRECTED 2026-07-15: firmed up with primary-source detail. WIPO published two international patent applications from Samsung Bioepis in early July 2026 covering hyaluronidase purification/manufacturing: WO2026/142299 (method for removing cleaved/truncated hyaluronidase) and WO2026/142300 (method for removing impurities via caprylic acid treatment and depth filtration). No specific target product named. Following public reporting of this on 2026-07-14, Alteogen issued a same-day rebuttal statement asserting its ALT-B4 is a materially different substance from any PH20-based enzyme and that products combining pembrolizimab with ALT-B4 (Keytruda Qlex) are protected until 2043, arguing biosimilar competitors could not lawfully substitute a different hyaluronidase. Alteogen shares fell intraday on 2026-07-13/14 on the news. Samsung Bioepis stated it has not finalized which product(s) the purification IP will be applied to and is not pursuing an external platform-licensing business.
